Notation: p(x) := Df(x)^#(ω(f(x))) = (ω(f x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x) is the pull-back form f^#ω. C^∞ means smoothness of order ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞), i.e. of every finite order.

1. (The compact set.) ω ∈ D^j(V) has compact support, so tsupport ω is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact), and tsupport ω ⊆ V. By the properness hypothesis, K := f⁻¹(tsupport ω) ∩ A is compact, and K ⊆ A ⊆ U.
2. (Thickenings.) K is compact, U is open and K ⊆ U, so there is δ₀ > 0 with cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define:
   - O := thickening (δ₀/2) K, open, with K ⊆ O (self_subset_thickening, as δ₀/2 > 0);
   - C := cthickening (δ₀/2) K, closed, with O ⊆ C (thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - s := thickening δ₀ K, open, with C ⊆ s (cthickening_subset_thickening', since 0 < δ₀ and δ₀/2 < δ₀).
   If K = ∅, all these sets are empty and the argument below still applies.
3. (The cut-off.) Smooth Urysohn (exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff with n = ⊤, applied to the open set s and the closed set C ⊆ s) gives a C^∞ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = s, and ζ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ C. Consequently:
   - 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1 everywhere, and ζ = 1 on O;
   - tsupport ζ = closure s ⊆ cthickening δ₀ K ⊆ U (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening);
   - cthickening δ₀ K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so its closed subset tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. ζ has compact support.
4. (p is C^∞.)
   - x ↦ Df(x) is C^∞ because f is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right, using ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞).
   - x ↦ ω(f(x)) is C^∞ as the composition of the C^∞ maps ω (a test form) and f.
   - B ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM B is C^∞. It sends a continuous linear map B : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q to the continuous linear map α ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap B on j-covectors, and it is analytic on the whole space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiff).
   - Since p(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Df(x)))(ω(f(x))), p is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.clm_apply).
5. (The test form.) Define η(x) := ζ(x)·p(x). η is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul). Also tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ (tsupport_smul_subset_left), so η has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right) and tsupport η ⊆ U by step 3. Hence η ∈ D^j(U) = TestFormOn U j, and η(x) = ζ(x)·p(x) for all x by definition.
6. (Support.) If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(f(x)) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Hence p(x) = 0, the pull-back of the zero covector being zero, and η(x) = 0. So support η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω). This set is closed, since f is continuous and tsupport ω is closed, so tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω) (closure_minimal).
7. (The open set.) Put N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), an open set. A ⊆ N: for x ∈ A, if f(x) ∈ tsupport ω then x ∈ K ⊆ O; otherwise x ∈ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω).
8. (η = p on N.) If x ∈ O ⊆ C, then ζ(x) = 1 and η(x) = p(x). If f(x) ∉ tsupport ω, then p(x) = 0 = η(x) by step 6.
9. Steps 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8 show that η, ζ and N have all the required properties. ∎

Smooth Urysohn on thickenings of K gives a C^∞ cut-off ζ with values in [0, 1], compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood O of K.
The pull-back p = f^#ω is C^∞ (B ↦ B^# is analytic), so η := ζ·p ∈ D^j(U) with tsupport η ⊆ f⁻¹(tsupport ω).
η = p on the open set N := O ∪ f⁻¹(ℝ^Q ∖ tsupport ω), which contains A.

Recall spt Z = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z), where zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all W with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and Z(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (“Z vanishes on W”). (F2′): by the reused lemma isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅. (Balls): for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, W := B_r(x) is open, closure W = B̄_r(x) (`closure_ball`) is compact (`isCompact_closedBall`); so W is admissible for zeroRegion as soon as B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and Z vanishes on W.

1. (Part (1).) Let x ∈ spt ∂Z, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∉ spt Z. Then x ∈ zeroRegion(Z): x ∈ W for some W open with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and Z vanishing on W. For φ ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W we have tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W (SimonGMT `tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), so ∂Z(φ) = Z(dφ) = 0. Thus ∂Z vanishes on W, W is admissible for zeroRegion(∂Z), and x ∈ zeroRegion(∂Z), contradicting x ∈ spt ∂Z. Hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (No openness of U is needed.)
2. (Part (2).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ K. The set U ∖ K is open (U open, K closed) and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ K (take half of a radius of a ball inside U ∖ K). Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, hence tsupport ω ∩ spt Z_j = ∅ for every j, so Z_j(ω) = 0 by (F2′); since Z_j(ω) → Z(ω) and limits in ℝ are unique, Z(ω) = 0. 3. (Part (3).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible (B̄_r(x) ⊆ U), x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. ∎

1. (|·| is continuous on Λⁿ(ℝ^P).)

EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ : ℝ^{m+1} ≃L (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) is WithLp.ofLp and its inverse is WithLp.toLp, so EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ (cons(s, x)) = Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) holds definitionally. Hence t(cons(s, x)) = (Fin.cons s _) 0 = s (Fin.cons_zero), and, since Fin.tail (Fin.cons s v) = v (Fin.tail_cons), tl(cons(s, x)) = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ x) = x. Both identities t(cons(s, x)) = s and tl(cons(s, x)) = x hold by definitional unfolding (rfl).
2. (Part (a).) By function extensionality it suffices to show G(cons(0, x)) = F₀(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^m. By step 1, G(cons(0, x)) is definitionally F₀(x) + 0·(F₁(x) − F₀(x)); and 0·v = 0 (zero_smul) and F₀(x) + 0 = F₀(x) (add_zero). Lean remark: simp does not rewrite EuclideanSpace.equiv _ _ (WithLp.toLp 2 _), so first restate the goal definitionally, `change F₀ x + (0 : ℝ) • (F₁ x - F₀ x) = F₀ x`, and then `rw [zero_smul, add_zero]`.
3. (Part (b).) Likewise, for x ∈ ℝ^m, G(cons(1, x)) is definitionally F₀(x) + 1·(F₁(x) − F₀(x)), which equals F₀(x) + (F₁(x) − F₀(x)) = F₁(x) (one_smul, add_sub_cancel; in Lean `change F₀ x + (1 : ℝ) • (F₁ x - F₀ x) = F₁ x` first). By funext, (x ↦ G(cons(1, x))) = F₁.

   (i) The map q ↦ Fin.tail q from (Fin (m+1) → ℝ) to (Fin m → ℝ) is C^∞: by contDiff_pi it suffices that each coordinate q ↦ q(i.succ) is C^∞, which is contDiff_apply.
   (ii) EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ and (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm are continuous linear equivalences, hence C^∞ (ContinuousLinearEquiv.contDiff). By ContDiff.comp, tl = (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm ∘ Fin.tail ∘ EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ is C^∞.

Source: steps 0(i)–0(v) and Step 1 (core estimate) of the supplied proof of comparison, with the constants of 0(iv) chosen before the maps; Steps 2–4 of that proof (the ε-argument) are not part of this child. Notation: dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ k ω ∈ D^{k+1}(ℝ^{m′}); its underlying form is, by definition, exteriorDerivative ω, so "compatible with (g, dω)" is literally the compatibility with (g, exteriorDerivative ω) occurring in (E0)/(E1). |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm. Lemmas used: compatible_form (iwl_sp_exists_compatible_testForm), support_lemmas (iwl_cr_support_lemmas), testform_bounded (br_la_testForm_covectorNorm_bounded) and affine_homotopy (dph_lpf_cmp_affine_homotopy).

Assume (Prod) and (SH), and write (E0), (E1), (Aff) for the three conjuncts of (SH). Fix m, m′, k, X, ω and L as in the claim (M(X) < ∞, the HEq boundary-mass hypothesis, 0 ≤ L).

1. (Data that do not depend on the maps.)
   (a) By (Prod) for m, k and X (M(X) < ∞) there is Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z).
   (b) By (Aff) for (m, m′, k) there is c ≥ 0 with the property stated in (Aff).
   (c) By testform_bounded with P := m′, n := k + 1, U := univ, applied to dω, there is C₁ > 0 with |dω(y)| ≤ C₁ for all y ∈ ℝ^{m′}.
   (d) Put B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0 (ENNReal.toReal_nonneg). Since M(X) ≠ ∞, ENNReal.ofReal B = M(X) (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal), so M(X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
   Now distinguish the cases k = 0 and k = j + 1 (in Lean: `cases k` after obtaining (a)–(d), which specializes them).

2. (Case k = 0.) Put C₀ := c·B·C₁; C₀ ≥ 0 as a product of nonnegative numbers. Let F₀, F₁, O, s, η₀, η₁ satisfy the hypotheses of the claim.
   (i) (The homotopy.) Let H := H[F₀, F₁] (in Lean: `set H : Eucl (m + 1) → Eucl m' := fun y => … with hH`, the lambda copied from (Aff), so that the properness hypothesis reads "H proper on cyl(spt X)"). affine_homotopy applied to F₀, F₁ and G := H (the equation G = H[F₀, F₁] being hH) gives (x ↦ H(cons(0, x))) = F₀, (x ↦ H(cons(1, x))) = F₁ and, as F₀ and F₁ are C^∞, H is C^∞.
   (ii) (Compatible form for dω.) Apply compatible_form with P := m + 1, Q := m′, j := 0 + 1, U := univ, V := univ, A := cyl(spt X) and f := H. Its hypotheses hold: univ is open, A ⊆ univ, H is C^∞ by (i), and for every compact K ⊆ univ the set H⁻¹(K) ∩ A is compact by the properness hypothesis on H. Applied to the test form dω it gives η′ ∈ D^{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and an open set N with cyl(spt X) ⊆ N and η′(y) = dω(H(y)).compContinuousLinearMap(DH(y)) for all y ∈ N (the remaining conclusions of compatible_form are not needed). Thus η′ is compatible with (H, dω) near cyl(spt X), with witness N.
   (iii) (Homotopy formula.) Apply (E0) to m, m′, X, Z and G := H, using M(X) < ∞, ProdChar(X, Z) (1(a)), H C^∞ and H proper on cyl(spt X), and then to ω, η₀, η₁, η′. (E0) requires η₀ to be compatible near spt X with (x ↦ H(cons(0, x)), ω); rewriting with the identity (x ↦ H(cons(0, x))) = F₀ from (i), which occurs in the argument of ω and inside fderiv, turns this requirement into the hypothesis that η₀ is compatible with (F₀, ω) near spt X (in Lean: `by rw [hend0]; exact hη₀`). In the same way the requirement on η₁ follows from (x ↦ H(cons(1, x))) = F₁ and the hypothesis on η₁. The requirement on η′ is (ii). Hence X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′).
   (iv) (Affine estimate.) Apply the property of c from 1(b), i.e. (Aff) for (m, m′, 0), to X, Z, F₀, F₁, O, s, L, B, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′. Its hypotheses are exactly: 0 ≤ s, 0 ≤ L, 0 ≤ B, M(X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B (1(d)), ProdChar(X, Z) (1(a)), F₀ and F₁ C^∞, O open, spt X ⊆ O, dist(F₁(x), F₀(x)) ≤ s and both derivative bounds for x ∈ O, F₀ proper on spt X, |dω(y)| ≤ C₁ for all y (1(c)), and η′ compatible near cyl(spt X) with (H[F₀, F₁], dω), which is (ii) since H is by definition the explicit lambda of (Aff). It gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L^0·B·C₁.
   (v) Hence |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| = |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L^0·B·C₁ = c·s·1·B·C₁ = C₀·s.

3. (Case k = j + 1: further data that do not depend on the maps.)
   (a) Apply the HEq hypothesis with this j and Y := X: k = j + 1 holds by rfl and HEq X X by HEq.rfl; so M(∂X) < ∞. Put B′ := M(∂X).toReal ≥ 0; as in 1(d), M(∂X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B′.
   (b) By (Prod) for m, j and ∂X ∈ D_j(ℝ^m) (M(∂X) < ∞) there is Z′ ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(∂X, Z′).
   (c) By (Aff) for (m, m′, j) there is c′ ≥ 0 with the property stated in (Aff).
   (d) By testform_bounded with P := m′, n := j + 1, U := univ, applied to ω, there is C₂ > 0 with |ω(y)| ≤ C₂ for all y.
   (e) By part (1) of support_lemmas with P := m, m := j, U := univ and Z := X, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X. Moreover spt ∂X = univ ∖ zeroRegion(∂X) is closed, because the zero region is open (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion; in Lean `isClosed_univ.sdiff X.boundary.isOpen_zeroRegion`).
   Put C₀ := c·L^{j+1}·B·C₁ + c′·L^j·B′·C₂; C₀ ≥ 0 since all factors are nonnegative.

4. (Case k = j + 1: the estimate.) Let F₀, F₁, O, s, η₀, η₁ satisfy the hypotheses of the claim, and let H := H[F₀, F₁] with the three facts of 2(i) from affine_homotopy.
   (i) (Compatible forms.) compatible_form as in 2(ii), now with j := j + 1 + 1 and applied to dω = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ (j + 1) ω, gives η′ ∈ D^{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and an open N ⊇ cyl(spt X) on which η′ is compatible with (H, dω). compatible_form with j := j + 1, the same P, Q, U, V, A, f and its hypotheses, applied to ω, gives θ′ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) and an open N′ ⊇ cyl(spt X) with θ′(y) = ω(H(y)).compContinuousLinearMap(DH(y)) for all y ∈ N′.
   (ii) (Homotopy formula.) Apply (E1) to m, m′, j, X, Z, Z′ and G := H, using M(X) < ∞, ProdChar(X, Z) (1(a)), ProdChar(∂X, Z′) (3(b)), H C^∞ and H proper on cyl(spt X), and then to ω, η₀, η₁, η′, θ′; the compatibility requirements on η₀ and η₁ follow from the hypotheses by rewriting with the endpoint identities exactly as in 2(iii), and those on η′ and θ′ are (i). Hence X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′).
   (iii) (First affine estimate.) The property of c from 1(b), i.e. (Aff) for (m, m′, j + 1), applied exactly as in 2(iv) to X, Z, F₀, F₁, O, s, L, B, ψ := dω, C := C₁ and η′, gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L^{j+1}·B·C₁.
   (iv) (F₀ is proper on spt ∂X.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^{m′} be compact. F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact by hypothesis, so (F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X) ∩ spt ∂X is compact, being the intersection of a compact set with a closed set (IsCompact.inter_right, 3(e)). Since spt ∂X ⊆ spt X, this set equals F₀⁻¹(K) ∩ spt ∂X (inter_assoc and inter_eq_right).
   (v) (Second affine estimate.) Apply the property of c′ from 3(c), i.e. (Aff) for (m, m′, j), to ∂X, Z′, F₀, F₁, O, s, L, B′, ψ := ω, C := C₂ and θ′. Its hypotheses hold: 0 ≤ s, 0 ≤ L, 0 ≤ B′, M(∂X) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B′ (3(a)), ProdChar(∂X, Z′) (3(b)), F₀ and F₁ C^∞, O open, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ O (3(e)), the distance and derivative bounds on O, F₀ proper on spt ∂X ((iv)), |ω(y)| ≤ C₂ for all y (3(d)), and θ′ compatible near cyl(spt ∂X) with (H[F₀, F₁], ω): take the same open set N′, which contains cyl(spt ∂X) because cyl(spt ∂X) ⊆ cyl(spt X) (if t(y) ∈ [0, 1] and tl(y) ∈ spt ∂X then tl(y) ∈ spt X). It gives |Z′(θ′)| ≤ c′·s·L^j·B′·C₂.
   (vi) Hence |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| = |Z(η′) + Z′(θ′)| ≤ |Z(η′)| + |Z′(θ′)| (abs_add_le) ≤ c·s·L^{j+1}·B·C₁ + c′·s·L^j·B′·C₂ = C₀·s.

5. In both cases C₀ ≥ 0 was chosen before F₀, F₁, O, s, η₀, η₁ (it depends only on m, m′, k, X, ω and L), and |X(η₁) − X(η₀)| ≤ C₀·s holds for all data satisfying the hypotheses. This proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Before the maps are chosen: Z with ProdChar(X, Z) from (Prod), c from (Aff) for (m, m′, k), C₁ > 0 bounding |dω| (testform_bounded), B := M(X).toReal with M(X) ≤ ofReal B; then case on k.

k = 0: C₀ := c·B·C₁. For H := H[F₀, F₁], affine_homotopy gives H(cons(0,·)) = F₀, H(cons(1,·)) = F₁ and H C^∞; compatible_form (A := cyl(spt X), f := H) gives η′ compatible with (H, dω) near cyl(spt X).
(E0), with the endpoint compatibilities rewritten via affine_homotopy, gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′); (Aff) gives |Z(η′)| ≤ c·s·L⁰·B·C₁ = C₀·s.

k = j + 1: M(∂X) < ∞ from the HEq hypothesis with Y := X, Z′ with ProdChar(∂X, Z′), c′ from (Aff) for (m, m′, j), C₂ > 0 bounding |ω|, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X and spt ∂X closed (support_lemmas); C₀ := c·L^{j+1}·B·C₁ + c′·L^j·B′·C₂.

compatible_form gives η′ (for dω) and θ′ (for ω); (E1) gives X(η₁) − X(η₀) = Z(η′) + Z′(θ′); (Aff) for X and for ∂X (F₀ proper on spt ∂X, θ′ compatible near cyl(spt ∂X) ⊆ cyl(spt X)) bound both terms, and their sum is ≤ C₀·s.
